rule_contract.note: Source of the frozen required-evidence text for all 8 rule IDs, including the explicit local-only wording for LLM-PRV-001/LLM-EVL-001 ('a model call elsewhere in the repository does not establish...') that action item 3 names, and the recognized resolved-inter-procedural allowance in LLM-IOH-001/LLM-VAL-001/LLM-AGY-001/LLM-DAT-001 that the other 4 represented rules carry.

explicit_action_item_3_contracts.LLM-PRV-001: requires an identifiable local model invocation (directly or via an observably-called local helper) before the result emission it anchors on; a model call 'elsewhere in the repository' does not establish this -- the contract recognizes no general cross-repository inference.
explicit_action_item_3_contracts.LLM-EVL-001: requires the case iteration, eligibility/exclusion filtering, aggregate calculation, and emitted result to form one locally traceable chain; 'a model call elsewhere in the repository does not establish evaluation applicability' and a locally assigned alias is accepted only when its lineage is directly observable.
explicit_action_item_3_contracts.LLM-EVL-002: requires the producer model/configuration and the judge model/configuration to both be resolvable and their identity equality (or inequality) determined without inferring an unrelated distinct judge from elsewhere in the repository.

derived_contracts_for_remaining_rules.LLM-IOH-001: the frozen rule contract itself already recognizes a 'same-function or deterministically resolved inter-procedural data path' -- i.e. cross-file resolution is in-contract at medium confidence, unlike the 3 named rules above. This document still asks the narrower architecture question (would today's single-file detector reach the decisive evidence, or does it need a capability it does not have) for consistency across all 34 rows.
derived_contracts_for_remaining_rules.LLM-VAL-001: same pattern: the contract recognizes 'a fully resolved supported inter-procedural flow' at medium confidence.

methodology_and_limitations: Every one of the 34 frozen evidence_scope entries in the golden opportunity manifest pins a single-point anchor (start_line == end_line in all 34 cases); none independently pins a second, distinct line for a correlated signal (e.g. a separate judge-configuration line for an EVL-002 opportunity whose anchor is the producer call). Whole-file source bytes for the golden cohort are not committed to this repository -- per protocol.md section 5 step 8, the source-evidence index retains only digests in public/internal artifacts inspected here, and no external repository source was fetched to fill that gap (fetching live external source was treated as out of scope for this action item and was not attempted).

Per discovery-anchor-contract-v1.9.json, each rule's candidate_normalization groups multiple contributing signals (producer, alias, helper, sink, judge, rubric, etc.) into one candidate anchored at a single canonical_locus line. That the methodology normalizes to one anchor does not by itself prove every contributing signal is textually co-located in the same file as the anchor -- the normalization is about where the finding is reported, not about the span of code that was read to support it. This document therefore treats a single-point anchor as inconclusive on its own, and only classifies an opportunity file-local when an independent, frozen corroborating signal is also present. Where no such corroboration exists, the item is recorded ambiguous/cross-module rather than assumed file-local by default.

Corroborating signals used, all drawn from committed v1.9 artifacts: (a) same-repository/same-rule opportunities that all anchor to one file, especially when their lines are textually adjacent (a strong same-block signal); (b) golden execution-evidence coverage counts (sourceFilesConsidered / sourceFilesWithLlmIndicators) that bound how many files in a repository could plausibly carry a second correlated signal; (c) the discovery-anchor-contract's own canonical_locus/candidate_normalization text for the applicable rule; (d) golden-manifest repository metadata (primary_surface, inclusion_reason) that names an architecture pattern (e.g. a declared graph/node evaluation framework, or a monorepo with separate app/package directories) independent of any specific line of code.

No repository metadata, coverage count, naming convention, or directory layout inspected for this document amounts to reading the defect's actual source code. A single committed anchor, by itself, is insufficient to establish that all required same-local-scope elements for a rule's contract are co-located in the anchored file, and is equally insufficient to establish that they are not; every row below is worded to that standard.

One golden repository's execution receipt (Ankitha-GS/rag-qa) additionally records that the origin no longer resolves on GitHub as of the most recent re-execution -- independent confirmation that live external re-inspection of golden source is not an available or reproducible substitute for the missing committed whole-file evidence in this cycle, reinforcing why this document does not attempt to fetch external source.

This is a structural, engineering-scoping conclusion, not a performance or ground-truth-correctness conclusion: it is not a claim about what the underlying repository code definitely does, and it does not relabel any opportunity's present/absent ground truth. This binary file-local/cross-module classification is a fallback bookkeeping label for a genuinely unresolved row, not affirmative architecture evidence about any of the 34 underlying repositories.

classification_definitions.file_local: All decisive evidence needed to satisfy the opportunity's rule-specific required-evidence checklist is inferred, with at least one corroborating signal beyond the single-point anchor itself, to be observable within the single file named in evidence_scope.path_or_reference.
classification_definitions.cross_module: The rule's required-evidence checklist plausibly or demonstrably needs evidence correlated from a second, different file than evidence_scope.path_or_reference (a separate producer/judge/config/orchestrator module, a separate presentation-layer file, or a separate package in a monorepo), based on a corroborating signal in the frozen artifacts.
classification_definitions.ambiguous: Per the operating instruction for this action item, ambiguous is recorded as classification=cross-module with ambiguous=true and owner_review_flag=true, used whenever the single committed evidence_scope anchor is, on its own, insufficient to establish that all required same-local-scope elements for the applicable rule are co-located in the anchored file -- the anchor alone is treated as insufficient to assert file-local, and asserting cross-module with confidence would equally overreach, so it is flagged for owner review rather than guessed. All 34 rows are recorded ambiguous under this definition; this binary classification is a mandated conservative fallback, not affirmative architecture evidence.
